title: God's Desire to Dwell With Us

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them. Make this tabernacle and all its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you." - Exodus 25:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the heart of the whole tabernacle project, and it is breathtaking: "I will dwell among them." The Almighty God, whose glory burned like fire on the mountaintop, wanted to live in the middle of His people's camp. Not far away on a distant peak, but right there among the tents, travelling with them wherever they went. God's desire has always been nearness.

Pause on how remarkable this is. God does not need a house. He was not seeking shelter. The tabernacle existed because God wanted to be present with His people in a way they could see and approach. Every detail of it was designed to make a way for a holy God to dwell among an unholy people without destroying them.

And this longing of God's reaches its climax in Jesus. John writes that the Word became flesh and "made his dwelling among us" (John 1:14) — literally, He tabernacled among us. God no longer dwells in a tent of goat hair; through His Spirit He dwells in His people themselves (1 Cor 3:16). And the story ends with God's dwelling place among His people forever (Rev 21:3). From Sinai to Bethlehem to eternity, the message is the same: God wants to be with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I truly grasp that God desires to dwell with me, not merely tolerate me?
How does God's presence with me change how I face today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, from the very beginning You have wanted to dwell with Your people. Thank You that through Christ You live in me. Let me never take Your nearness for granted. Amen.
